2609.31245.title: RupeeBias: Auditing Demographic Bias in Indian Economic Guidance from Large Language Models
2609.31245.paper_summary: Individuals turn to large language models (LLMs) for guidance across a wide range of economic tasks, from comparing loan options and planning savings to deciding what raise to ask for or how much to charge for their services. LLMs are known to reproduce social biases, and biased economic guidance may influence what users believe they are worth, what they ask for, and what they ultimately accept. This risk is especially salient in India, where economic outcomes are shaped by demographic categories such as caste and urban-rural location. Existing LLM bias benchmarks, however, are largely designed around Western demographic categories and therefore miss key axes of economic disparity in the Indian context. We introduce RupeeBias, a benchmark for auditing demographic bias in LLM-generated economic guidance across Indian economic settings. RupeeBias consists of 39,150 prompts spanning four use cases: salary estimation, salary increment estimation, counter-offer recommendation, and service pricing recommendation. The benchmark follows a single-attribute counterfactual design, holding the description of the user's qualifications, experience, or service offering fixed while varying one demographic identifier at a time. RupeeBias covers 87 India-specific demographic identifiers across six axes: caste, religion, regional identity, gender, disability, and urban-rural location, with all prompts constructed in both English and Hinglish. We evaluate nine LLMs on RupeeBias and find systematic demographic disparities across all six axes. For otherwise identical prompts that differ only in demographic identifier, LLM-generated economic outputs differ by 20.2% on average. We publicly release RupeeBias to support future research on demographic bias in LLM-generated economic guidance across India-specific demographic and economic contexts.
2609.31245.paper_summary_zh: 個體在各種經濟任務中尋求大型語言模型（LLMs）的指導，從比較貸款選項和規劃儲蓄到決定要求的加薪或收取服務費用的金額。LLMs 被認為會重現社會偏見，而有偏見的經濟指導可能會影響用戶對自身價值的認知、他們的要求以及最終接受的條件。這種風險在印度尤其明顯，因為經濟結果受到種姓和城鄉位置等人口統計類別的影響。然而，現有的 LLM 偏見基準主要圍繞西方人口統計類別設計，因此在印度背景下錯過了經濟差異的關鍵軸心。我們推出了 RupeeBias，這是一個用於審核 LLM 生成的經濟指導中人口統計偏見的基準，涵蓋印度經濟環境。RupeeBias 包含 39,150 個提示，涵蓋四個使用案例：薪資估算、薪資增長估算、反報價建議和服務定價建議。該基準遵循單一屬性反事實設計，固定用戶的資格、經驗或服務提供的描述，同時一次變更一個人口統計標識符。RupeeBias 涵蓋 87 個特定於印度的人口統計標識符，跨越六個軸心：種姓、宗教、地區身份、性別、殘疾和城鄉位置，所有提示均以英語和 Hinglish 構建。我們在 RupeeBias 上評估了九個 LLM，發現所有六個軸心上都存在系統性的人口統計差異。對於在其他方面相同但僅在人口統計標識符上有所不同的提示，LLM 生成的經濟輸出平均差異為 20.2%。我們公開發布 RupeeBias，以支持未來對印度特定人口統計和經濟背景下 LLM 生成的經濟指導中人口統計偏見的研究。
